findings.title: NPE when the 'Clients' resource-type resource does not exist
findings.body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when no per-client resource is found the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and immediately passes the result to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` without a null check. `getResourceTypeResource` returns `null` in several reachable cases: the realm has an admin-permissions client but `realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled()` is false (so `supportsAuthorizationSchema` returns false), or the `Clients` resource simply does not exist (e.g. a realm whose admin-permissions client was created before this schema change, see the `init()` early-return). Also, if `findByResource` happens to be non-empty while `resource` is null, `new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server)` dereferences null. The result is a NullPointerException in authorization checks, i.e. HTTP 500 on ordinary admin client endpoints instead of a clean allow/deny. Add a null check that returns `false` when the fallback resource is missing.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns the resource-type name and misses per-client grants
findings.body: `getClientsWithPermission` iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and adds `resource.getName()` to the result. Per-client resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner)` without ever setting a resource type, so they are never returned by `findByType`. The only resource with type `Clients` is the "all clients" resource created in `init()`, whose name is the literal string `"Clients"`. Consequently this method returns either an empty set or `{"Clients"}` — never real client ids — while callers of `ClientPermissionEvaluator.getClientsWithPermission(scope)` expect a set of client ids (the V1 implementation strips the `client.resource.` prefix and returns ids). Grants on individual clients are invisible to those callers and the bogus `"Clients"` entry can be mistaken for a client id.

findings.title: canExchangeTo now throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking legacy token exchange when V2 is enabled
findings.body: `ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo(...)` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. Because `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns `ClientPermissionsV2` (previously it returned the V1 `ClientPermissions`), the legacy token-exchange flow, which calls `AdminPermissions.management(session, realm).clients().canExchangeTo(client, targetClient, token)`, will now blow up with an unchecked exception and return HTTP 500 whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled together with the token-exchange feature. Either keep delegating to the V1 behaviour or make the caller aware that token exchange permissions are not available in V2 and return a proper deny/400 instead of an unhandled runtime exception.

findings.title: Management-permissions admin endpoints return 500 with V2 enabled
findings.body: `isPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel)`, `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)`, `getPermissions(ClientModel)` and `resource(ClientModel)` all throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. These are invoked directly by the admin REST endpoints `GET`/`PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/management/permissions` (`ClientResource.getManagementPermissions`/`setManagementPermissionsEnabled`). Since `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns this class, enabling `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` turns those endpoints from working (V1) responses into unhandled runtime exceptions, i.e. HTTP 500. A deliberate 400/404 (e.g. `ModelValidationException`/`NotFoundException`) would be the appropriate contract for "not supported in V2".

findings.title: Listener guard checks the V1 feature, so client removal still hits V2 code paths
findings.body: The provider-event listener body is now guarded by `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`, but the code inside calls `management(session, realm)` which dispatches to `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled. If both preview features are enabled at the same time (nothing prevents this), removing a client executes `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)`, which now throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (ClientPermissionsV2), aborting client deletion with an internal error. The guard should also exclude the V2 feature (or the listener should explicitly use the V1 `MgmtPermissions`). Additionally, gating cleanup on the V1 feature means that when the feature is turned off, previously created V1 permission policies for removed roles/clients/groups are left behind as orphans.

findings.title: No migration of new scopes/resource for already initialized admin-permissions clients
findings.body: `init()` returns early when `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null`, so realms that already had admin permissions enabled before this change never get the newly introduced scopes (`configure`, `map-roles-client-scope`, `map-roles-composite`) nor the `Clients` resource-type resource. On such realms, creating a Clients permission fails: `getScope()` throws `ModelValidationException("Scope [configure] does not exist.")`, and `getOrCreateResource()` throws `ModelException("No scopes found.")` when building the per-client resource (HTTP 500), and `hasPermission()` in ClientPermissionsV2 cannot find the fallback `Clients` resource. Some upgrade/initialization path is needed to add missing schema scopes and resource-type resources to existing admin-permissions clients.

findings.title: getResourceName not extended for the Clients resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName` resolves friendly names only for the `Users` resource type ("All users" / username). For the newly added `Clients` resource type it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is null for resources created by `getOrCreateResource` (only name and owner are set). As a result, permissions created for clients will be reported without a resolvable name in representations, unlike user permissions, and there is no "All clients" label for the resource-type resource.

findings.title: Javadoc on require* methods describes a return value for void methods
findings.body: `requireView()` (line 98) is documented as "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}." and `requireViewClientScopes()` (line 103) as "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}." Both methods are `void` and, consistently with the other `require*` methods in this interface, throw `ForbiddenException` when the corresponding `can*` check fails. The Javadoc therefore documents behaviour that does not exist and should read "Throws ForbiddenException if ... returns {@code false}".

findings.title: Dead code and unused imports left from copy/paste
findings.body: The class contains a private, never-called `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` method (line 262), an unused `logger` field (line 51) and unused imports/static imports (`Scope`, `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `EvaluationContext`, `AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE`). This is leftover from copying the V1 implementation; it produces compiler warnings and suggests an evaluation-context customization that is not actually applied. It should be removed.

findings.title: New map-roles-client-scope scope is untested
findings.body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` is added to the Clients resource type and `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles` is implemented, but no test exercises it (tests only cover `manage`, `configure`, `view`, `map-roles` and `map-roles-composite`). Likewise there is no test for the all-clients `configure` permission or for a negative-logic (deny) client permission. Without coverage, regressions in the client-scope role mapping evaluation would go unnoticed.

findings.title: testManageOnlyOneClient mutates shared realm state without cleanup
findings.body: `testManageOnlyOneClient` renames `myclient` (`setName("somethingNew")`), removes one of its default client scopes and adds it as an optional scope, but registers no `realm.cleanup()` task to restore it. The realm/client are shared by the other tests in this class (only scope permissions are cleaned in `@AfterEach`), so the mutated client-scope assignment and name leak into subsequent tests, making the suite order-dependent and potentially flaky (e.g. other tests index into `getDefaultClientScopes()`).
